patch.value: Let SDK extension read commands opt into universal context output controls

Real calendar adoption for PR1439 exposed an enhancement opportunity: the optional read command correctly omits universal output-budget flags from its contract, and the core guard refuses them because read-output policies currently enumerate built-in surfaces. Add an explicit public SDK declaration and structured output contract allowing package authors to opt read commands into projection, omission and budget controls while preserving fail-closed behavior for writers and undeclared commands. Current calendar JSON behavior and shipped core read controls remain valid.

Installed Node and Bun read extensions opt in through a public SDK contract and preserve omission and budget refusal semantics; write and undeclared extension commands continue to reject read-only controls; aliases agree with availability and flag contracts.
Custom package read commands can declare and reuse the same truthful context projection and budget primitives as core readers, with runtime contracts exposing only supported flags.
